newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse cautious ahead of Greenspan speech.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse cautious ahead of Greenspan speech.

text.p: Belgian shares closed higher on Monday, clawing back earlier losses, but investors remained cautious ahead of Wednesday's semi-annual commentary on the U.S. economy by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Dealers said the blue-chip Bel-20, which closed up 0.46 percent at 2,104.48, was helped by afternoon buying of index-linked products and some investors taking comfort from the Dow's slight rebound.
Trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck said the launch of index-linked products would most likely push the Bel-20 to a 2,150-2,200 range in coming weeks.
Market attention focuses on Franco-Belgian banking group Dexia which closed up 125 francs at 3,495 francs, after the group said it would make an announcement.
The group announced after the bourse closed that it would take a 40 percent stake in Italy's Crediop and that the price would be between 1.6 and 1.9 billion French francs.
"The Bel-20 was extremely calm today except for Dexia," said Paul de Lophem.
Elsewhere financials were the Bel-20's main gainers, with Kredietbank ending up 2.72 percent at 12,275 francs and Generale Bank up 1.64 percent at 12,400 francs.
"Maybe people are buying Belgian financials because of possible takeover stories circulating, I see no other reason for the rises," said analyst Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen.
Financial group Fortis AG gained 2.41 percent to close at 5,940 francs.
Elsewhere the Bel-20's main loser, steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, closed down 1.44 percent at 20,600 francs.
"Bekaert is likely to show bad results, and it is not only a question of results but also sentiment in the market and there is overproduction in every sector of Bekaert," said de Lophem.
Chemical producer Tessenderlo which closed down 50 francs at 15,900, said after the bourse closed that its 1996 net profit was down 17.2 percent.
Gert De Mesure said a failure for Tessenderlo so far to announce any takeover deal had recently made speculators dump the share.

Elsewhere oil and chemical group PetroFina failed to profit from announcements of oil and gas discoveries in Vietnam, and the restoration of most of its war-damaged base in Angola's port city of Soyo. It closed unchanged at 12,275 francs.
